drafts.title: Improve ride comfort on broken pavement so bumps feel muted
drafts.description: When driving on broken or patched pavement at typical suburban speeds, occupants experience noticeably less vibration and jolting — the car feels composed and comfortable rather than harsh.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized broken-pavement route (speeds 30–50 mph) the average vertical seat acceleration RMS shall be ≤ 1.2 m/s² and at least 85% of a 20-person user panel rates ride comfort ≥ 7/10.
assumptions: Standardized test route and instrumentation are defined (benchmarked to current 5 Series test protocol).
Improvements may use adaptive suspension, revised damping, chassis NVH tuning and tire choices available for the successor model.
uncertainties: Improvements may trade off with very sporty handling; exact tuning targets depend on final vehicle weight and wheel/tyre options.

drafts.title: Offer a long-range variant that delivers at least 600 miles real-world range
drafts.description: Customers who prioritize maximum driving range can buy a variant that provides long-distance driving capability without frequent recharging stops.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A long-range variant achieves ≥ 600 miles real-world range (EPA-equivalent combined/test-cycle and verified on a sustained 70–75 mph highway run) on a single full charge under normal ambient conditions.
assumptions: Higher energy-density cells (e.g., >300 Wh/kg) or increased usable pack capacity will be available to meet energy requirements.
Customers accept trade-offs in weight, packaging and cost for a long-range variant.
Range validation will use EPA-equivalent procedures and a sustained highway verification run.
uncertainties: Achieving 600 miles depends on future cell energy density, vehicle mass, and aerodynamic efficiency; calendar and cycle life impacts must be evaluated.

drafts.title: Make fast-charger compatibility and route charging planning obvious and fast to use
drafts.description: When planning a trip or en route, customers can quickly find compatible fast chargers, see connector type and availability, and add recommended charging stops to the route without confusion.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a 200–300 mile simulated trip across multiple networks the car’s route planner lists compatible chargers (connector type and network) for each recommended stop; 90% of test users can plan and accept a charging stop within 2 minutes and the system finds at least one compatible fast charger within 10 miles of the route for 95% of test routes.
assumptions: Access to up-to-date network and charger metadata (connector type, adapter requirements and live availability) from charging providers or aggregators is available.
UI and route-planning integration can present compatibility info and one-tap add-to-route flows.
uncertainties: Third-party charger data quality and live-availability accuracy vary by region and may limit performance in some areas.

drafts.title: Reduce distracting wind noise above highway speeds so cabin stays quiet
drafts.description: At sustained highway speeds the cabin noise from wind should remain low and unobtrusive so conversations and media are not disturbed.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Closed-window cabin A-weighted noise level shall be ≤ 68 dB(A) at 75 mph on a standardized highway track; in addition, at least 80% of a 20-person blind panel rates wind noise as 'not distracting' during a 30-minute highway drive at 70–80 mph.
assumptions: Measurement uses a defined microphone position(s) per current OEM NVH standards.
Improvements may require aero sealing, mirror/trim optimization and improved door sealing.
uncertainties: Actual noise levels depend on final mirror design, glass, roof options and wheel/tyre choices.

drafts.title: Make lane-keeping assist steer smoothly in curves without abrupt corrections
drafts.description: When lane-keeping assist is active the system supports the driver with steady, predictable steering in bends and does not produce sudden, sharp corrections that startle the driver.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In repeated curved-road tests up to 70 mph the system’s steering correction rate shall not exceed 2°/s and lateral jerk shall be ≤ 0.2 m/s³; during these tests at least 85% of drivers rate steering behaviour as 'smooth' (≥4/5).
assumptions: Tests use representative highway curves and standard tyre/vehicle configurations.
Driver takeover prompts and system limits will be tuned to prioritize smoothness while maintaining safety.
uncertainties: Behavior must remain safe across vehicle speeds, driver inputs and road geometries; edge cases (e.g., abrupt cut-ins) may still require firm corrective actions.

drafts.title: Show charging state clearly at the charge port so owners can check at a glance
drafts.description: When plugged in, the charge-port indicator communicates the charging state (charging, full, error) with a visible, color-coded signal and the same state is clearly shown in the vehicle UI so users understand status within seconds.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Charge-port indicator provides at least three distinct, color-coded states (charging, full/topped, fault) visible from 2 meters; in a 5-second glance test 95% of users correctly identify the state and the same state is reflected in the instrument cluster or app.
assumptions: Indicator visibility is tested with common lighting conditions and with adjacent parked vehicles.
UI/icons use standard color semantics and are tested for color-blind accessibility.
uncertainties: Indicator visibility can be affected by aftermarket covers, installation height and surrounding lighting in some parking situations.
